personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: A vector store and an edge function is a lot of machinery for a search box. It's fluff to me unless the plain search still answers when that machinery is down.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: If every agent finds the same law from its own words, the teams stop drifting from the rules.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: An agent that finds the right rule writes less slop, as long as it can still be checked against the id it cites.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Agents finding laws from plain questions means my ideas get built the way the product works.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: I ask in customer words, not the law's words: meaning search is what makes it useful to me.

objection.text: A vector store and an edge function is a lot of machinery for a search box. It's fluff to me unless the plain search still answers when that machinery is down.

rounds.fit: Fits the PMs and the lead engineer best, the skeptical back-end developer worst, until the word-search fallback was made explicit.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: The word search stays as the fallback and the mode says which ran: the machinery earns its keep if the eval holds.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: A measured eval as the acceptance test, and duplicate ids fixed: I can trust the answers.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Exact ids first is good; I'll believe the rest when agents cite the right law.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Eleven of twelve natural questions in the top five is the bar I wanted.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Paraphrases count in the eval, which is how I actually ask.

rounds.fit: Every persona at 3 or more; the skeptical developers wait on the eval's numbers.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: The word search still answers when the vectors are down, so it costs nothing to try; I'll trust it once the eval holds after deploy.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Every agent finding the same rule from different words keeps the teams aligned, and the eval script lets me check it.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Read-only and exact ids first; I'll judge it when agents cite the right law in their pull requests.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Agents now understand the product the way I describe it, not only in its own words.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: I can ask in customer words and still land on the right rule.
